cards.card: Visa Platinum Card (including HSBC easy Credit Card)
HSBC Pulse UnionPay Dual Currency Diamond Credit Card

note: Hong Kong's largest retail banks are HSBC, Bank of China (Hong Kong), Hang Seng Bank and Standard Chartered. HSBC and Hang Seng are written. Bank of China (Hong Kong)'s card pages publish no fee table or key facts statement this research could find (its product listing has no fee links, 2026-10-30); Standard Chartered Hong Kong's key facts statement (effective 27 April 2025) was fetched, but its tables don't come out of the PDF in an order that can be read card by card, and it isn't written. HSBC's key facts statement for its credit cards (June 2025, read again 2026-10-30): retail purchases and cash advances 31.8% a year (the annualised monthly 2.65%); interest-free up to 56 days; the minimum payment the fees and charges billed plus 1% of the statement balance, at least 300 dollars, plus any overdue or over-limit amount (written as 1% with a 300 floor; the billed fees aren't added); annual fees for the primary card: Premier MasterCard and Red Credit Card waived permanently, Visa Signature and EveryMile 2,000 (EveryMile's spending waiver isn't stated in figures and isn't written), Visa Platinum (with the easy card) 1,800, Visa Gold and Gold MasterCard 600, Visa and MasterCard 300, the iCAN Card 300, the Pulse UnionPay dual-currency Diamond 1,800 and the UnionPay dual-currency card 300; the US dollar Visa Gold costs 80 US dollars and its statement is paid in full each month (written as a charge card). From 1 August 2025 a cash advance costs 1% with a floor of 150 dollars (20 US dollars on the US dollar card); spending in another currency 1.95% (1% on the UnionPay dual-currency cards, outside renminbi and Hong Kong dollars); a late payment 300 dollars or the minimum payment if lower (the cap isn't written); over the limit 90 dollars a cycle (12 US dollars); a returned payment 100 dollars (13 US dollars). The renminbi sub-accounts' fees, the paper-statement and bill-payment fees and the 1% charge on Hong Kong dollar spending abroad aren't written. Hang Seng Bank's key facts statement for its credit cards, in its card applications' important notes (PPL871, March 2026, read 2026-10-30), with the notes for the Visa Infinite, World Mastercard, Visa Signature, enJoy and MUJI cards: 2.67% a month on purchases and cash advances, written by the month; interest-free up to 56 days; the minimum payment 300 dollars or the sum of fees and charges, the overdue minimum, the excess over the limit and 1% of the rest, whichever is higher (written as 1% with a 300 floor); annual fees for the primary card by type: Visa Infinite and World Mastercard 6,000, both waived for the first three years for every applicant (seven for full-time students, not written); Visa Signature 2,000, Platinum 1,500, Gold 600, Classic (with the Fortune Mastercard) 300; the Prestige World and MMPOWER World Mastercards waived; the Visa Platinum, Platinum Mastercard, UnionPay Platinum, UnionPay credit card, Visa Signature, enJoy and renminbi cards are offered to every applicant with the annual fee waived for good, written as costing nothing; the MUJI Visa Platinum 1,500 with its first year waived for every applicant (for good for a first Hang Seng card, a condition not written); the US dollar Visa Gold 78 US dollars; the renminbi cards 1,500, 600 or 300 yuan, waived. The World Mastercard and US dollar Visa Gold are paid in full each month (written as charge cards). A cash advance costs 0.5% with a floor of 100 dollars (13 US dollars; 100 yuan); spending in another currency 1.95% (1.2% on the UnionPay cards); a late payment 330 dollars (42 US dollars) or the minimum if lower (the cap isn't written); over the limit 200 dollars a cycle (26 US dollars); a returned payment 120 dollars (16 US dollars). The university, Jockey Club and Club Marina Cove membership cards, open only to their members, aren't written; nor is the paper-statement fee.
